issues.description: The problem statement and the template define Developer.attend(course:) with a single parameter of type Course? (optional). The solution implementation changes the method signature to attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool) by adding an extra Boolean parameter. This signature mismatch is structural and could confuse students (and tests) because the method they are instructed to implement does not match the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signatures across artifacts. Either remove the extra parameter from the solution's method (change solution to: func attend(course: Course?) { ... }) so it matches the problem statement and template, or update the problem statement and template to require the additional forCredit: Bool parameter if that parameter is intended. Prefer removing the extra parameter in the solution to preserve the exercise instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define an instance method attend(course:) on Developer with signature attend(course: Course?). The solution implementation unintentionally changes the method signature to attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool), adding a second parameter. This creates a naming/signature mismatch: students implementing attend(course:) from the instructions/template will not find the same method in the solution and may be confused about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Developer.attend method match the problem and template signature by removing the extra parameter: change func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool) { ... } to func attend(course: Course?) { ... } (or provide a default value for the new parameter, e.g. forCredit: Bool = false, to preserve backward compatibility).
